Subject: Custody/Residency assurances for our Private VPC deployment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we proceed to legal and procurement, our compliance team has a couple of specific asks about the Private (VPC) deployment model:

1) Chain of custody: we need an exported, time-stamped audit trail that proves which tenant artifacts (models, inference logs, snapshots) were present and when, and which actions (delete/export/snapshot) were taken and by which principal.
2) Residency guarantees: can you confirm that data and snapshots will remain in the US region we select and won't be replicated cross-region without explicit auth?
3) Deletion timelines & proof: after we request a tenant wipe, what are the steps, and how long until data is unrecoverable? We also need a signed manifest/attestation we can archive.
4) Backups & third-party copies: do you ever send copies to vendor systems (monitoring, support sandboxes)?

Can you provide a short Q&A or checklist we can attach to our security review? Samantha from CloudCorp is helping coordinate.

Thanks,
Rajiv

Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear asks. I’ve outlined the short-form answers below and attached a one-page custody checklist and our KMS rotation schema. Monica (Ops) and Karthik (Security) are cc'd for any deeper evidence or formal attestation.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Chain of custody: Redwood Private exposes an immutable audit stream for tenant-level operations. Events include actor, API call, resource id, and timestamp. We provide exportable JSONL logs filtered by tenant id and time window. These logs are stored in the customer VPC under a tenant-owned logging bucket when requested (or can be pushed to your SIEM via secure transfer).
- Residency: By default tenant artifacts (object storage, snapshots, KV caches) live in the single region you select at provisioning. Cross-region replication is OFF by default and must be enabled via an explicit account-level toggle; we record that toggle in the audit stream.
- Deletion & attestations: Wipe flow is three phases — (1) tenant-initiated soft-delete (marks objects + snapshot manifests for deletion), (2) background compaction & overwrite where storage blocks are zeroed or reallocated, (3) crypto-shred if customer-managed keys are present (KMS key destroy/rotation). We produce a signed deletion manifest (hash list + timestamps + operator id) within 72 hours of the wipe request and provide an attestation statement signed by Redwood’s security officer upon request. Final low-level irrecoverability (crypto-shred) timing depends on storage and crypto key lifecycle — typical completion window: up to 30 days for full destruction in standard configurations; accelerated options are available if you use customer-managed keys.
- Backups & third-party copies: Redwood does not proactively copy tenant data to external vendor sandboxes. We may create ephemeral diagnostic snapshots for support only with explicit customer opt-in; these are time-limited, logged, and require a documented justification.

Attachments: vpc-data-custody-checklist.xlsx (checklist + export steps), kms-rotation-schema.pdf (describes KMS key lifecycle options).

If you want the formal attestation, let me know the signatory name/title you need and we’ll route to Legal/Security. Also happy to run through the checklist on a short call.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

Rajiv — forwarding a short formal confirmation and next steps. I’m adding the official attestation template and scheduling a 30-minute call to walk through your checklist and produce the signed manifest once you initiate a wipe.

Key confirmations (formal):
- The 72-hour deletion manifest will include: tenant id, object ids (hashed), timestamp, responsible operator id, and a SHA-256 bundle hash. The manifest will be digitally signed by Redwood’s security officer.
- Long-term snapshots are stored in the tenant’s configured region by default. Any cross-region replication for backups requires an explicit written change by a named customer admin and will be recorded in the tenant audit stream.
- If you elect customer-managed keys (CMK), Redwood will perform crypto-shredding by destroying the CMK per the configured KMS policy; we will include the CMK destroy event in the attestation.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the contact for the attestation (name/title/email) and whether you require notarization.
2) If you want accelerated destruction timelines we can enable the accelerated purge workflow (note: there may be operational constraints for slow-moving archival media).
3) Proposed call: Mon, Jan 16 09:00 PT — calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/meet/mt-custody-20280114
